title: Extract the documentation machinery from abacus into this repo
description: Move the funnel/docs-doctor tooling out of its abacus incubation into its own home, then finish the unbuilt half here. Contents to migrate: the operator-approved spec PROPOSAL-funnel-and-docs-doctor.md (v20), tools/probe_executor.py, tools/docs_doctor.py, tools/test_probe_executor.py, tools/test_docs_doctor.py, and the fixture harness patterns. Still unbuilt: jot and jot-review (spec build step 3, gated on experiment 5). Abacus keeps its governed CONTENT (doc-meta blocks, docs/README.md corpus index, evidence index, archive pointer index, its membership file, its adapter) and consumes the tools as optional dev tooling. TIMING: do not move anything until the in-flight abacus worker lands; the operator pauses abacus dev during the migration. Children carry the deliverables; the design field carries the three settled decisions.
design: THREE SETTLED DECISIONS (operator, 2026-08-12). (1) DEPENDENCY DIRECTION - abacus does NOT pin jot. abacus pins br/bv/herdr because its product code wraps their CLI and JSON with no in-band version negotiation, so a silent format change breaks an adapter at runtime. jot is different in kind: zero product-runtime coupling, and every jot event carries schema_version with bad_schema_version as a typed refusal, so a version-skewed drain fails closed BY THE FORMAT. That is a better pin than a lock file because it travels with the data rather than with each consuming repo. abacus records at most a minimum-version line in its agent contract. This keeps abacus lean toward its actual goal: an execution engine for draining a bead backlog. (2) JOT PINS BR - the pin belongs with the consumer of the unstable interface, not two levels up. br's CLI and JSON have no in-band versioning and jot wraps them, so jot carries the version, binary checksum, mismatch policy, and compatibility record. Coupling inventory: two read-only CLI sites today (br --no-db show for forward bead citations in docs_doctor, and for the tracker_status probe kind in probe_executor), a direct read of the tracked issues JSONL for reverse citations (coupling to beads STORAGE format, not its CLI), and jot-review's future write side (br create with --external-ref, plus the br list reconciliation read). CRITICAL PRECISION: requires-br means declared dependency for full function, NOT refuses-to-start. The code already degrades loudly when br is absent (built and fixtured in review rounds 5-8) and that robustness is kept - tracker-free checks (structure, metadata, indexes, supersession, archive) still run and still catch real defects. A missing hard dependency must be loud, not fatal-at-import. (3) MANIFEST SPLIT - class definitions are standard, membership is per-repo. Measured against the two live manifests, exactly five things differ: managed_globs, managed_files, historical_files, the standing class files list, and whether the architecture class is present. Everything else is byte-identical: all class grammars (prd/adr/evidence regexes, unique_by, calendar_date_group, roles), the three index singletons, inflight_globs, discovery, and both semantics literals. So the tool SHIPS the class library at a version and each repo declares only membership - roughly seven lines (conforms_to, protected_mainline_ref, and the five lists) instead of thirty copied ones. conforms_to supersedes the earlier idea of bolting a schema_version onto a copied blob: the repo names the class-library version it conforms to and the tool refuses a version it does not implement, giving docs-doctor the same in-band self-description jot events already have. DEFECT THIS EXPOSED: the skills repo manifest omits the architecture class entirely; under the standard-library model that class exists everywhere and simply has no members where there is no architecture doc, exactly as prd has none in abacus today.
notes: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-12 - MVP FIRST, FIX AS WE USE. This governs every build in this repo, not just one bead. Stop building contingencies on top of contingencies for failure modes that have not happened and are unlikely to. Find errors through dogfooding and handle them then, with observed evidence. What triggered the ruling: sable-note and sable-review are a WORKING product (123 lines of bash plus a skill) covering the same capture-then-curate shape, and the v20 spec made that exponentially more complicated across twenty versions and eighteen review rounds without anyone ever opening the existing tool to establish what was inadequate about it. The working agreement rule verify-the-seam-before-you-draft was applied religiously to code seams and never once to the product. Consequence recorded on jot-met.7: jot and jot-review build at sable parity plus four cheap improvements; the crash-safety machinery is demoted to design of record. Consequence for future work here: a spec being approved does not make it a build order, and a review round finding real defects does not prove the artifact under review should be that large - the ceremony-budget rule tests round productivity within a chosen scope and is blind to over-scoping. docs-doctor is the exception that earned its cost: it is net-new, and it caught real defects on first contact with the real corpus.

title: Repo foundation: agent contract, corpus governance, cross-review lane
description: Stand up this repo's own identity before anything migrates. Deliverables: (a) AGENTS.md naming the remote (git@github-personal:DylanDelliColli/jot.git - the default SSH key has no write access, the github-personal alias is required), the br prefix jot-, tree-residency rules (tree holds current state, git history is the archive, transition guard on every overwrite or delete, docs/history/README.md pointer index, one review file per cycle, one shift report per lane), and the rule that this repo's tools are the product; (b) README.md as front door plus a validation ledger; (c) docs/README.md corpus index and docs/history/README.md pointer index; (d) CLAUDE.md alias symlink to AGENTS.md; (e) .gitignore for __pycache__. CRITICAL, do not skip: establish a CROSS-REVIEW LANE. Every one of the thirty defects in the docs-doctor build was caught by an adversarial Codex reviewer working from a pane in the abacus cwd; this repo has no such lineage yet. Either open a Codex pane with this repo as cwd or record an explicit cross-repo review arrangement in AGENTS.md. Without it the jot build loses the discipline that produced the tool's quality. title: Migrate the spec with a provenance block pointing at abacus history
description: Move PROPOSAL-funnel-and-docs-doctor.md (operator-approved v20) from the abacus root into this repo. The move must add a PROVENANCE block, because the spec's entire justification lives in abacus's git object store and this repo has no history of it: ten adversarial spec-review rounds archived as pointer rows in abacus docs/history/README.md (recoverable via git show COMMIT:PATH from the abacus checkout), the taxonomy consultation advisory, and ten implementation-review rounds whose findings are named by ID in abacus commit messages between b2ac26b and 54f74c1. Without that pointer a fresh agent here can read WHAT the spec says but cannot recover WHY - which is exactly the recoverability guarantee the tree-residency contract exists to provide. Record the abacus repo identity plus the coordinate form so the rows stay resolvable. Gotcha: abacus's own archive pointer rows keep working forever regardless of this move because they are (commit, blob) coordinates rather than tree paths - the review history does NOT migrate, only a pointer to it does. Acceptance: the spec is in this repo with a provenance block; a reader following it can recover at least one archived review round from the abacus checkout; abacus no longer carries the spec at its root.
notes: SCOPE CLARIFICATION after the 2026-08-12 MVP ruling: the spec migrates as the DESIGN OF RECORD, not as a build order. Its capture-funnel sections describe machinery that jot-met.7 explicitly does not build (event fold, publish protocol, two-observation gate, patch artifacts, landing conjunction, attempt state machine, reconciliation). When migrating, add a status banner to the spec saying so, naming jot-met.7 as the authority on what is actually built, so a fresh agent cannot mistake the document for an implementation contract. The docs-doctor half of the spec IS implemented and frozen; only the funnel half is aspirational.
close_reason: Closed without doing it - operator ruling 2026-08-13. PROPOSAL-funnel-and-docs-doctor.md is the 817-line v20 artifact produced across roughly eighteen adversarial review rounds, and it is the canonical example named in the operator's own MVP-first ruling: that machinery was specified to replace sable-note, a 123-line bash script nobody opened across twenty spec versions. A five-arm controlled review of it (identical inputs, varying only the reviewer mandate) had every bloat-mandated arm conclude it retains no MVP deliverable and should be deferred wholesale, while a normal adversarial review of the same document produced eight real defects and zero scope challenges - it would have produced v21. Importing it would place that document in the repository whose north-star non-goals were just rewritten to refuse its machinery by name (non-goal 6: no event identifiers, canonical digests, publish protocols, folds, two-observation gates, attempt state machines, or crash reconciliation), and every future agent in jot would read it as local design authority. It is also unnecessary: docs-doctor is already built and tested, so the code and its suite are the authority and the spec merely describes them. What this bead actually wanted is one line, not a migration - record in jot's AGENTS.md or README that the design history for the documentation machinery lives in abacus-v1 (the spec at repository root, tools under tools/). If a specific rationale is ever needed - why doc-meta carries the fields it carries, why the severity taxonomy is shaped as it is - extract those paragraphs then, against a real question.

title: Port the four structural docs-doctor checks into jot; leave abacus-v1 untouched
description: Port a MINIMAL docs-doctor into this repo. Scope narrowed by operator ruling 2026-08-13: only the four structural checks migrate, and nothing is deleted from abacus-v1. PORT: abacus-v1/tools/docs_doctor.py reduced to check_metadata (doc-meta role/lifecycle blocks), check_corpus_index (every managed doc has its index row), check_corpus_index_agreement (index and manifest agree), plus the supporting machinery those three need - manifest load and validation, classify_docs, discover_tracked, classify_root_and_modules, collect_managed, and path confinement. Port the matching subset of abacus-v1/tools/test_docs_doctor.py. The suite is 2305 lines across eleven checks with a shared harness and manifest fixtures, so this is a genuine split rather than a copy; the operator has explicitly authorized that cost as cheaper than debugging bloated features later. DO NOT PORT the other seven checks: check_supersession, check_probes, check_bead_citations, check_historical_bytes, check_archive_index, check_reverse_citations, check_evidence_index. They are deferred, not rejected - the operator considers probes, bead-citations and reverse-citations valuable but not MVP. They stay in abacus-v1 and are revived by porting them later, against an observed need. DO NOT PORT probe_executor.py or test_probe_executor.py. Verified 2026-08-13 by following the import graph: docs_doctor.py imports ProbeExecutor once at line 29 and uses it in exactly one place, check_probes at line 1063. With that check deferred the executor has no consumer here. THIS DISSOLVES THE OWNERSHIP PROBLEM raised in the rename-impact note: because probe_executor does not move, PROPOSAL-knowledge-fixture/generate.py in abacus-v1 keeps importing its local copy unchanged, so the acceptance criterion requiring abacus experiments 2-4 to re-run green against an installed tool is MOOT and is removed. There is nothing for an abacus-side lane to produce and no need to authorize one. DO NOT DELETE abacus-v1/tools/. The prior 'retire the abacus copies' step is withdrawn. That directory is now the archive holding the seven deferred checks and the executor, and abacus-v1 is a frozen parts bin. The original 'two copies is a drift defect' rationale does not apply: an archive that never changes cannot drift, and jot's copy is authoritative only for the four checks it carries. SKILLS DEPENDENCY - decide explicitly, do not discover: skills/AGENTS.md currently invokes abacus-v1/tools/docs_doctor.py (repointed 2026-08-13 at skills 2b1efe3 after the rename broke the old path). Its only live findings today are two reverse-citations rows on skills-xg9, and that check is NOT in this port. So skills either keeps using the eleven-check archive copy or moves to jot's four-check copy and accepts losing that signal. Record the choice in skills/AGENTS.md as part of this bead. Acceptance: the four checks plus their ported tests are green from jot's repo root; docs-doctor runs clean or degraded-with-known-findings against jot itself; abacus-v1 is untouched; skills/AGENTS.md states which copy it uses and why.
notes:
CROSS-REPO HANDSHAKE - who deletes from abacus. This bead spans two repositories and two lanes, so the boundary must not be ambiguous. The jot-side lane (w1H:p1) is scoped READ-ONLY on the abacus checkout and must stay that way: three other lanes share that tree. Sequence: (1) the jot lane copies the tools in, gets both suites green here, and reports ready-to-retire; (2) an ABACUS-side lane performs the deletion of the abacus tools directory and the spec, because it owns that tree, knows what else is in flight there (a worker was still running in a lane-yx3 worktree at planning time), and the deletion interacts with abacus bead abacus-yi9 whose docs-doctor gate points reference those paths; (3) that same abacus lane re-runs the knowledge-fixture experiments 2-4 against the installed tool - that green run is the migration acceptance evidence and it can only be produced from the abacus checkout. Do NOT lift the read-only restriction to make this simpler; the handshake is cheaper than a shared-tree accident. Nothing here starts until the in-flight abacus worker lands and the operator clears it.

RENAME IMPACT 2026-08-13 (jot-d9m intake, not yet adjudicated - operator input needed before this bead is claimed). The abacus repository was renamed abacus-v1 and a fresh unrelated abacus was created in its place. Verified this session: all four tool files, PROPOSAL-knowledge-fixture, and commit 54f74c1 are in abacus-v1; the new abacus is a Rust workspace with its own bead store on an ab- prefix namespace; abacus-yi9 is still OPEN in the abacus-v1 tracker. Four consequences. (1) Mechanical: every abacus path in the description above means abacus-v1. (2) The phrase that the knowledge fixture stays in abacus is now ambiguous and should read abacus-v1. (3) The handshake rationale is largely void: it existed because three lanes shared the abacus tree and a worker was live in a lane-yx3 worktree, but abacus-v1 is now a frozen parts bin where nothing moves, so the shared-tree-accident risk that justified both the read-only restriction and the two-lane sequence no longer holds. (4) Sharper problem - the acceptance evidence now has no owner. Steps 2 and 3 require an ABACUS-side lane, and a frozen repo has none. The operator must either authorize this lane to act in abacus-v1 for the deletion and the experiments 2-4 re-run, or re-scope acceptance so the migration does not depend on evidence nobody is positioned to produce. Do not silently drop the experiments criterion - it is the only end-to-end check that the migrated executor still serves its real consumer.

comments.author: w1p1-orchestrator
comments.text: SCOPE NARROWED by w1:p1 on operator ruling, 2026-08-13. This answers the four consequences raised in the RENAME IMPACT note, so that note can be treated as resolved rather than pending. (1) and (2) mechanical path corrections stand - every abacus path meant abacus-v1. (3) The two-lane handshake is void as the note suspected, and is now moot for a second reason: nothing is deleted from abacus-v1 at all, so no abacus-side lane action is required and the read-only restriction never needs lifting. (4) The acceptance-evidence ownership problem is DISSOLVED rather than adjudicated. It existed because migrating probe_executor.py would have rewired PROPOSAL-knowledge-fixture/generate.py's import, requiring experiments 2-4 to be re-run from the abacus checkout by a lane that no longer exists. Following the import graph shows probe_executor has exactly one consumer in docs_doctor - check_probes - and that check is deferred, so the executor does not move, generate.py is untouched, and there is no evidence to produce. The criterion is removed, not silently dropped. WHY ONLY FOUR CHECKS: the operator's stated scope for docs-doctor is that it enforces the docs structure a repository declares, preventing markdown-soup. Of the eleven implemented checks, four serve that; the rest do tracker cross-referencing (bead-citations, reverse-citations), git archaeology (historical-bytes, archive-index, supersession) or claim verification (probes). Those are valuable and explicitly deferred rather than rejected. Telling detail from the live run against skills: both findings it produced came from reverse-citations, the check furthest from the stated scope. ALSO NOTE abacus-yi9 in the abacus-v1 tracker has docs-doctor gate points referencing tools/ paths. Because nothing is deleted there, those gates keep working and this bead no longer interacts with that bead at all.

comments.author: w1p1-orchestrator
comments.text: EVIDENCE PRESERVED from the README validation ledger before that section was deleted 2026-08-13. Two observations recorded there are real findings about reverse-citations and they are the strongest support for keeping that check deferred out of jot's port - the check does not merely observe the tracker, it shapes what gets written in it. (1) During jot-gtz an interim docs-doctor run reported four findings instead of two because the tracking bead quoted the unmigrated spec's filename twice, and reverse-citations emits one finding per occurrence; the resolution was to REWORD THE BEAD so the check would stop counting. (2) During jot-8ou, deleting the archived shift report raised a third finding because the already-CLOSED bead jot-d9m cited the report by bare filename; the resolution was to rewrite that closed bead's citation into the path-at-commit form the tool accepts. In both cases a tracker record was edited to satisfy a documentation check rather than because the record was wrong. That is a genuine cost of the check and it was only visible from dogfooding. It does not argue for dropping reverse-citations permanently - the operator considers it valuable - but it does mean any future promotion out of deferral should decide deliberately whether a check that edits tracker prose is wanted, and should probably gain a way to reference a filename without triggering a finding.

title: Split docs-corpus.json into a shipped class library plus per-repo membership
description: Implements settled decision 3 on the epic: ship the class grammar with the tool, leave each repo declaring only its membership. Today each consuming repo copies about thirty lines of manifest of which only five things legitimately vary (managed_globs, managed_files, historical_files, the standing class files list, and whether the architecture class is present); the class grammar, index singletons, inflight_globs, discovery and semantics literals are byte-identical across live manifests. SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-13, inherited from jot-met.3's old scope. THE CONSUMER SET CHANGED and is now the load-bearing correction: the two live consumers were jot and abacus. abacus was renamed abacus-v1 and frozen - its manifest must NOT be regenerated, it is an archive - and the new abacus is a Rust workspace with no docs-corpus.json and no docs-doctor. So the live consumers are jot and the skills repo, and skills' participation is conditional on skills-r44, which decides whether skills keeps invoking the eleven-check archive copy or moves to jot's four-check port. Do not regenerate a membership file for any repo that is not actually running this tool. SHIP ONLY WHAT THE PORTED CHECKS CONSUME: the four ported checks are check_metadata, check_corpus_index, check_corpus_index_agreement and the classification and confinement they need. Of the three index singletons, only corpus-index serves a ported check - evidence-index serves check_evidence_index and archive-index serves check_archive_index, both deferred. Classes and settings that exist only for deferred checks stay in the abacus-v1 archive with them and return if those checks are ever promoted. DELIVERABLES: (a) ship the class library with the tool, versioned; (b) reduce the per-repo file to membership plus conforms_to and protected_mainline_ref; (c) make the tool REFUSE a conforms_to version it does not implement, as execution_error - this is docs-doctor's in-band self-description and it replaces the earlier idea of bolting schema_version onto a copied blob; (d) regenerate membership files only for repos actually running the ported tool. Gotcha: the manifest validator enforces exact top-level keys and frozen semantic literals; both move into the class library and the membership validator needs its own exact-key rule so the fail-closed property survives the split. Acceptance: every repo actually running the ported tool works from a membership-only file and produces the same findings the ported checks produced before the split; a bad conforms_to yields execution_error; the fixture covers unknown-version refusal and membership-only validation.

title: Externalize the remaining abacus-specific identifiers
description: Two hardcoded consumer-repo identifiers make the tool less portable than its clean cross-repo runs suggest (verified 2026-08-12 against abacus commit 54f74c1): MODULE_RE at docs_doctor.py line 34 hardcodes the abacus module-contract path shape, and BEAD_RE at line 37 hardcodes the bead:abacus- forward-citation prefix - so a bead:jot- or bead:skills- citation in any other repo is SILENTLY unchecked. The skills repo's cross-run looked clean partly because these regexes matched nothing. Move both into the per-repo membership file from jot-met.4 (a module path pattern and a tracker ID prefix). Scope note per settled decision 2: this does NOT abstract the tracker vendor - br is a hard requirement - so the externalized surface is only per-repo CONVENTIONS (ID prefix, module path shape), not a pluggable tracker interface. Speculative vendor abstraction is refused until a non-br consumer actually exists. Acceptance: a bead: citation using this repo's own prefix is checked in this repo; a fixture pins that a foreign-prefix citation is not silently ignored; no consumer-repo identifier remains in tool source.
close_reason: Closed as moot for the narrowed port, 2026-08-13, not because the defect was wrong. This bead externalizes two hardcoded consumer-repo identifiers, and reading the tool shows BOTH serve only checks deferred out of jot-met.3's port: BEAD_RE (docs_doctor.py:37) is used at line 1145 inside check_bead_citations, and MODULE_RE (line 34) at line 1336 inside _reference_form, which belongs to the reverse-citations machinery. Neither is touched by the four ported checks. Confirmed the ported code is clean: the only occurrences of the string abacus in the whole tool are those two regexes plus one bead citation in a docstring, and classify_root_and_modules does not use MODULE_RE - it determines modules by other means, so classification ports with no portability defect. The original finding stands and is real: a bead:jot- or bead:skills- citation is SILENTLY unchecked by those regexes, which is why the skills cross-run looked cleaner than it was. That defect travels with check_bead_citations and check_reverse_citations into the abacus-v1 archive and is a PRECONDITION of ever promoting either check out of deferral - a promoted check that silently matches nothing is worse than an absent one. Settled decision 2 is unaffected: br is a hard requirement and this was never about abstracting the tracker vendor, only per-repo conventions. Its blocking dependency on jot-met.3 was removed before closing, since the port no longer carries the code this fixes.

title: Record the br surface jot-review wraps
description: Implements settled decision 2: the pin belongs with the consumer of the unstable interface. br's CLI and JSON carry no in-band version negotiation and this repo wraps them, so this repo carries the record - abacus does not pin jot in turn. SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-13 by the same operator ruling that narrowed jot-met.3, whose old scope this bead inherited. RECORD: br version, release asset, binary sha256, mismatch policy, and a dated compatibility record under docs/compatibility/, following the abacus provider-lock shape (the abacus-v1 .abacus/providers.lock.toml br entry is the model; abacus pinned br 0.1.45 with binary sha256 a3b59c6bde363efe251c28a7908d169f7b5671a22894e9577d253983750339e3, verified against the installed binary). THE ONLY OPERATION TO RECORD IS br create with --external-ref, used by jot-review when the operator promotes a note into a bead. That is the entire br surface jot wraps after the narrowing. DROPPED FROM THIS BEAD, because each existed to serve a check that is now deferred out of the port: br --no-db show for forward citations and the tracker_status probe (served check_bead_citations); the br list reconciliation read and the append-only comment surface and close_reason retention behavior (served reverse-citations and its unrepairable-prose severity cap). Verified 2026-08-13 by reading the tool: br is invoked at exactly one site in docs_doctor.py, line 1148 inside check_bead_citations, with its error helper at 1125. None of the four checks being ported - check_metadata, check_corpus_index, check_corpus_index_agreement, and the classification and confinement they need - touches the tracker at all. ALSO DROPPED: the missing-br loud-degradation fixture. It proved that tracker-dependent checks degrade rather than abort, and the ported set contains no tracker-dependent check, so there is nothing for it to prove here. The behavior stays in the abacus-v1 archive with the checks it protects, and returns with them if they are ever promoted out of deferral. STILL TRUE AND STILL THE POINT: requires-br is a declared dependency for FULL FUNCTION, not refuses-to-start. jot capture is pure filesystem and must keep working with no br installed; only jot-review's promotion step needs it, and a missing binary there is an operator-visible failure at the moment of promotion, not a silent one - jot-review is human-gated by non-goal 5, so there is no unattended path for a provider mismatch to corrupt. Acceptance: the compatibility record exists with a verified checksum and names br create --external-ref as the wrapped operation; jot capture demonstrably works with br absent.

title: Build jot and jot-review as a braindead-simple MVP (sable-note/sable-review parity plus four cheap improvements)
description:
Build the capture funnel at MVP scope. The v20 spec remains the design of record but is NOT the build order: its crash-safety machinery is demoted per the operator ruling of 2026-08-12 and gets built only when an observed failure demands it.

BASELINE TO MATCH: sable-note is 123 lines of bash that appends a timestamped block (cwd, git branch, short rev, observation text) to a daily markdown file. sable-review is a SKILL, not code: it reads those files, classifies each observation as edit-doc / file-a-bead / discuss / discard, proposes diffs, and archives processed entries after operator approval. Read both before writing anything - the entire reason this bead exists at MVP scope is that twenty spec versions were written without anyone opening the working product they replace.

BUILD - jot (capture). A single command that writes ONE FILE PER NOTE into a queue at the repository git-common-dir. Fields: the observation text, optional --file, --symptom, --repro, --why, plus automatic created_at, repo-relative cwd, HEAD short rev, and branch. JSON, one object per file, filename doubles as the note id. Plus a list subcommand showing pending notes. A plain write is fine; if temp-then-rename is free in the chosen language use it, but do NOT build a publish protocol. Target size is the same order as sable-note.

BUILD - jot-review (curation). A SKILL in the sable-review mould, operator-invoked, human in the loop for every disposition. Reads pending notes, presents them, and on operator decision either files a bead via br create, proposes a documentation edit, discards, or defers. Marks the note processed (move to a processed subdirectory is sufficient). Because a human is the gate, there are no automated effects to make safe.

THE FOUR IMPROVEMENTS OVER THE SABLE PAIR, all cheap, all the actual justification for building this at all: (1) one file per note rather than appending to a shared file - this is the entire concurrency advance at the ten-worker scale target, and it is a one-line difference; (2) JSON rather than prose so the curator and any tooling can parse notes reliably; (3) --file/--symptom/--repro promoted from prose convention to real fields, which is what the global capture rule already asks for in words; (4) the queue lives at the repo git-common-dir rather than one global directory, so notes stay with the repository they concern and survive worktree teardown. (5) One genuine jot-review improvement worth keeping: when a note becomes a documentation change, run docs-doctor after applying it so the corpus is verified rather than assumed - sable-review had no such check.

EXPLICITLY NOT BUILT, demoted to design of record in the spec: the seven-event fold (amend, question, answer, observed, intent, applied, final); ULID identifiers and canonical-JSON digests with duplicate collapse; the publish protocol (create-exclusive temp, fsync, no-clobber link, EEXIST reduction, quarantine); drain flock and concurrent-drain safety; the two-observation gate; content-addressed patch artifacts and the five-condition landing conjunction; the attempt state machine with aborts and absence proofs; idempotent bead promotion with external-ref crash reconciliation; the 28-entry typed error vocabulary; and experiment 5 crash matrix in full. Every one of those defends an unattended automated drain that does not exist and a crash window of well under a second.

ACCEPTANCE: dogfooding, not a fixture matrix. The tools are installed and used for real capture and curation in this repo and in abacus. Failures found in use become beads with the observed evidence attached. A small smoke test that capture writes a parseable note and that list shows it is sufficient; do not build a crash-injection suite.

title: Build jot capture in Python (split from jot-met.7)
description: Build the jot capture command only; jot-review the skill stays in jot-met.7. Split rationale: capture touches neither docs-corpus.json (jot-met.4), nor abacus identifiers (jot-met.5), nor br (jot-met.6), so it carries none of jot-met.7 real blockers and can land now to start producing the dogfooding evidence that jot-met.7 acceptance and the NORTH-STAR kill criteria both require. Language decision (operator, 2026-08-12): Python, matching the stdlib-only tools migrating in jot-met.3; revisit the repo language at jot-met.3, not here. Build tools/jot.py, a single stdlib-only Python CLI, executable, no third-party dependencies. Writes ONE FILE PER NOTE as JSON into the queue at git-common-dir/jot/pending so notes stay with their repository and survive worktree teardown. Fields: observation text plus optional --file --symptom --repro --why, plus automatic id, created_at, repo-relative cwd, HEAD short rev, and branch. A list subcommand prints pending notes. Write temp-then-rename via os.replace since it is two lines in Python; do NOT build a publish protocol. Pins two gaps jot-met.7 left open: note id format is timestamp plus pid plus 6 hex chars, chosen because ULIDs are explicitly excluded and the ten-worker target makes same-second collisions likely; and --why ships as written in jot-met.7 though it is the one field the global capture rule does not ask for. Test spec: tools/test_jot.py, stdlib unittest, real filesystem and real git repos via tempfile, no mocks. Cases: capture writes parseable JSON with every automatic field; optional fields appear only when passed; two notes in the same second do not collide; queue resolves to git-common-dir from a subdirectory and from a linked worktree; list shows pending notes and is empty-safe; outside a git repo exits nonzero with a clear message. Acceptance: suite green, and a real note captured in this repo by dogfooding.
close_reason: tools/jot.py landed stdlib-only; suite 22/22 green from the repo root; docs-doctor unchanged at degraded with the same 2 planned-output findings; dogfooded by installing on PATH and capturing three real observations in this repo

title: Migrate tool-side beads and sweep bead: citations
description: Bead IDs are prefix-bound, so migration is create-in-destination plus close-in-source-with-a-pointer, not a move - and every citation of a migrated ID goes stale. SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-13, inherited from jot-met.3's old scope. DELIVERABLES: (a) migrate the open tool-side beads from the skills repo, principally skills-9v3, which currently owns this extraction and carries its settled decisions in notes and design - this epic supersedes it, so close it with a pointer here; (b) leave closed beads alone - abacus-42w and abacus-e8v are closed with their evidence and belong to abacus-v1's history, which is frozen; (c) sweep bead citations for any migrated ID and update or annotate them; (d) abacus-yi9 stays where it is - it covers abacus's own AGENTS.md unit, that repo is now abacus-v1 and frozen, and nothing in this epic touches it. WHAT CHANGED: the forcing function for (c) is gone. The sweep was justified because the forward-citation check flags a missing ID as degraded and would surface stale citations anyway - that is check_bead_citations, which is deferred out of the port, and it is the single site where docs_doctor invokes br (line 1148). The old acceptance criterion, that docs-doctor reports no unresolved forward citations across three repos, is therefore UNVERIFIABLE by the ported tool and is removed rather than silently retained. The sweep is still worth doing on its own merit: a stale bead id in prose is a broken reference for a human or an agent regardless of whether a tool flags it. It is just no longer machine-enforced, so scope it by hand and stop when the open beads are consistent. Also note the repo set is smaller than when this was written: abacus-v1 is a frozen archive and the new abacus has its own tracker on the ab- prefix with no relationship to jot ids, so the sweep covers jot and skills. Acceptance: no open bead is stranded in a repo that no longer owns its work, and no open bead in jot or skills cites a migrated id that no longer resolves.
